newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South African union group welcomes Mandela speech.
newsitem.headline: South African union group welcomes Mandela speech.

text.p: South Africa's largest trade union federation Cosatu welcomed President Nelson Mandela's frank admittance of government's shortcomings and the will to correct them.

Cosatu said in reaction to Mandela's opening of parliament speech earlier on Friday that it also applauded government's commitment to a major expansion of health services, nutritional schemes, access to drinking water, land distribution and security of tenure for farmworkers.
"The president's speech contained a candid acknowledgement of certain shortcomings and a determination to correct these.

"These included an inability to spend effectively on social services and housing, insufficient economic growth to absorb the unemployed, and the need for more focused attention on crime," Cosatu said in a statement.
It said it shared the president's view that effective delivery of these and other measures required a "far reaching transformation of the public service".
Cosatu also welcomed the president's commitment of government to the National Framework Agreement on restructuring state assets and his call to parastatal management to respect this process.
The National Framework Agreement was signed early last year and relates to processes to be followed in privatising state concerns.
